explanation: A struct in C is a user-defined data type that allows grouping of variables of different types into a single unit. It is used to create complex data structures, improving code organization and readability by representing real-world entities as collections of attributes.
syntax: struct StructName { type member1; type member2; };
example_explanation: This program defines a struct named Point with two integer members, x and y. In the main function, an instance of Point is declared, values are assigned to its members, and then printed to the console, demonstrating how the struct groups related data and allows access to its members via the dot operator.

extraction_metadata.source: The C Programming Language - Kernighan & Ritchie
